name: Sabal

project_scope.selection_mode: 2026-10-10 Genus Comparison Builder; extend existing Arecaceae family lesson
project_scope.native_range_note: Do not infer target-county PASS from Texas-wide distributions; range review remains independent.

shared_genus_traits: Solitary unarmed palms with fan-shaped, costapalmate leaves: a central costa extends into the blade rather than ending abruptly at the petiole.
Fibrous sheathing leaf bases, long unarmed petioles and a hastula (flap at the upper petiole/blade junction).
Small bisexual flowers borne in branched inflorescences among leaves; flowers with three sepals, three petals and six stamens.
Dark, usually one-seeded, rounded to flattened-rounded mature fruits.

look_here_first.cue: Follow the leaf petiole into the fan: locate the costa and hastula. Then compare an adult stem, loose segment-edge fibers, and fruit diameter at the SAME SCALE.
sequence: Confirm a costapalmate leaf and unarmed petiole; this gets you into the Sabal lesson.
On mature plants, look for a persistent above-ground trunk versus leaves arising near ground level; do not stop here.
At the petiole-blade junction, measure the hastula and assess the length/curvature of the costa; check segment margins for threadlike fibers.
If reproductive material exists, compare inflorescence length and branching relative to leaves and measure multiple ripe fruits.

comparison_matrix.Sabal minor: Usually subterranean; crown often appears stemless, but some old plants develop an aerial stem.
comparison_matrix.Sabal mexicana: Usually conspicuous aerial trunk, about 20–35 cm diameter in the FNA treatment.
comparison_matrix.interpretation: Fast initial split only; young S. mexicana and exceptional trunked S. minor overlap.

comparison_matrix.Sabal minor: Weakly costapalmate, nearly flat; segment margins usually without loose threadlike fibers.
comparison_matrix.Sabal mexicana: Strongly costapalmate and curved; segments commonly filiferous (threadlike fibers).
comparison_matrix.interpretation: Use intact adult leaves; damage or age can remove fibers.

comparison_matrix.Sabal mexicana: Acute to acuminate hastula about 9.5–15.5 cm long.
comparison_matrix.interpretation: Measured structural separator; show scale and exact junction, not a distant leaf.

comparison_matrix.Sabal minor: Usually erect, much longer than leaves; 2 orders of branching excluding the main axis.
comparison_matrix.Sabal mexicana: Usually arching, about as long as leaves; 3 orders of branching excluding main axis.
comparison_matrix.interpretation: Compare flowering/fruiting adult plants; wind, damage and cultivation affect apparent length.

comparison_matrix.Sabal minor: About 6.4–9.7 mm across; brownish black, usually spheroid.
comparison_matrix.Sabal mexicana: About 14.8–19.3 mm across; black, often oblate-spheroid.
comparison_matrix.interpretation: High-value nonoverlapping published ranges; compare multiple ripe fruits with ruler.

overlap_cautions: An above-ground trunk does NOT automatically exclude S. minor; FNA notes large emergent forms. A small trunkless juvenile does NOT prove S. minor.
Cultivated palms, planted outside natural range, and possible interspecific hybrids should not be labeled as wild local native occurrences.
Do not infer species from leaf color, crown size, or plant height alone; favor measured hastula and ripe fruit plus mature leaf architecture.
FNA notes a possible hybridization hypothesis for a Brazoria County population; this is not proof of hybrids in Hays County.

realistic_lookalikes.name: Nolina (e.g., Nolina texana in source pool)
realistic_lookalikes.separate: Nolina has long narrow strap leaves in a rosette, not a broad costapalmate fan with a costa and hastula; flowers in many small clusters rather than palm fruits.

realistic_lookalikes.name: Yucca species in source pool
realistic_lookalikes.separate: Yucca has stiff simple linear blades, not a segmented costapalmate fan; large bell-shaped flowers and dry/fleshy capsules differ from Sabal drupes.

realistic_lookalikes.name: Other cultivated fan palms
realistic_lookalikes.separate: Do not assume any fan palm is Sabal. Check petiole armature, costa/hastula, leaf segment folding and mature fruits; keep cultivated look-alikes as provisional until keyed.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched whole adult plants with base exposed, ground line marked and crown visible.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.overlay: label aerial trunk vs subterranean stem; include exception warning

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched intact adult leaves photographed from comparable angles; macro of segment edges.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.overlay: arrow costa; label loose marginal threads present/absent

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched adaxial petiole-to-blade junction macros with centimeter ruler.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.overlay: trace hastula; mark rounded vs acute tip and measured length

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Whole inflorescence with leaves in same frame, plus detail of branch hierarchy.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.overlay: count branching orders, indicate inflorescence vs leaf length

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: At least 3 ripe fruits per species side-by-side with millimeter scale; include fruiting panicle context.
diagnostic_photo_checklist.overlay: mark equatorial fruit diameter and published range
